description: Reusable proof prerequisites for proof-carrying Type-4 frontier packets. Target packets cite these fact_id values; packet-local models may add only packet-specific current status.

evidence_requirement_vocabulary.focused-executable: A focused positive or hard-negative expectation must exercise the fact boundary.
evidence_requirement_vocabulary.formal-or-mechanized: A formal proof, proof obligation, or machine-checked model must justify the rewrite precondition.
evidence_requirement_vocabulary.source-evidence: The source program must expose evidence for the fact; names alone are not enough.

accepted_evidence: ordered integer literal bounds
asserted Guard(BoundOrder) evidence on a dominating exiting inverse guard, for example if hi < lo then raise/return/throw before the clamp
asserted Guard(BoundOrder) evidence on a positive branch guard, for example if lo <= hi then evaluate the clamp and the other branch exits
facts.detector_admission_implication: Does not admit a real clamp pair by itself; the paired members must also satisfy numeric-clamp.integer-domain.
implementation_guidance: Represent only dominating exiting inverse guards and positive branch guards as bound-order evidence.
Reject parameter naming, non-exiting checks, swapped bounds, and wrong min/max nesting.
rejected_evidence: parameter names such as lower/upper or minimum/maximum
non-exiting guard expressions
swapped bounds or wrong min/max nesting
facts.summary: The lower bound must be proven <= the upper bound before min(max(x, lo), hi), max(min(x, hi), lo), ternary clamp, and library clamp forms can share a Clamp value.
facts.title: Clamp bound order

accepted_evidence: integer literals
asserted integer parameter/domain evidence on each clamp operand
language/type evidence that excludes float, NaN, and non-total-order behavior
facts.detector_admission_implication: Does not admit a real clamp pair by itself; the paired members must also satisfy numeric-clamp.bound-order.
implementation_guidance: Gate clamp canonicalization to integer-domain operands.
Keep language domains that can include floats or NaN outside exact clamp admission.
rejected_evidence: Python dynamic numeric parameters without integer-domain evidence
TypeScript/JavaScript number domains
Go cmp.Ordered or other generic ordered domains that can include floats
facts.summary: Clamp canonicalization is restricted to integer-domain operands so float/NaN-sensitive min/max and comparison-chain forms stay closed.
facts.title: Clamp integer domain

accepted_evidence: comparison predicates whose results are booleans
the same element variable and the same literal/value coordinates on both sides
a boolean context where operand values are not observed
language or source evidence that excludes overloaded, value-returning, or effectful boolean operands
facts.detector_admission_implication: Does not admit a quantifier/loop convergence by itself; source identity, purity, counterexample-loop, and vacuous-truth facts are separate requirements.
implementation_guidance: Normalize De Morgan only when operands are proven boolean values.
Reject value-returning boolean contexts, overloaded comparison semantics, and predicate calls unless separate effect/purity evidence exists.
Attach new language surfaces by emitting boolean-operand evidence, not by adding language-specific detector branches.
rejected_evidence: value-returning and/or operands whose value, not only truthiness, is observed
overloaded comparison or predicate calls with effects
changed predicates such as x != 0 or x != 1
facts.summary: A De Morgan rewrite may be used only when both sides operate on proven boolean operands, not on language-specific value-returning boolean expressions.
facts.title: De Morgan over proven boolean operands

accepted_evidence: a universal quantifier/all/every surface over a single element predicate
an explicit loop whose only counterexample branch returns literal false
matching predicate coordinates between the quantifier and the loop counterexample
short-circuit order that stops at the first counterexample
facts.detector_admission_implication: Does not admit a loop/quantifier convergence by itself; vacuous truth, source identity, predicate purity, and any boolean rewrite facts remain separate.
implementation_guidance: Model only loops where the counterexample branch is the sole early false exit.
Keep extra loop control, observed loop effects, and unsupported body shapes closed until separate evidence exists.
Pair this fact with quantifier.vacuous-truth before admitting an all/every-style surface.
rejected_evidence: counterexample branches that return non-false payloads
loop bodies with extra observed effects, break, continue, else effects, or unsupported control
predicate-coordinate changes between the quantifier and the loop
facts.summary: A universal quantifier can match an early-return loop only when the loop is a pure counterexample scan that returns false at the first not-P element.
facts.title: Universal quantifier as counterexample loop

accepted_evidence: the quantifier surface returns true for an empty input
the explicit loop falls through to literal true after exhausting the same input
no loop else block, final payload, or post-loop effect changes the empty-input result
facts.detector_admission_implication: Does not admit a quantifier/loop convergence by itself; it only closes the empty-input boundary for a separately proven counterexample loop.
implementation_guidance: Treat empty-input behavior as a first-class proof fact, not as a side effect of loop-shape matching.
Keep loops that return false or a payload after exhaustion outside all/every admission.
Require this fact whenever a universal quantifier surface is matched to an explicit loop.
rejected_evidence: fallthrough returns false or a non-boolean payload
post-loop code changes the empty-input result
collection APIs with non-vacuous empty behavior
facts.summary: Universal quantifier rewrites must preserve the empty-input result: no counterexamples means true.
facts.title: Universal quantifier vacuous truth

accepted_evidence: the quantifier and explicit loop consume the same local iterable binding or receiver place
no reassignment or mutation changes the source between the two forms
the quantifier element and loop element refer to the same traversal coordinate
facts.detector_admission_implication: Does not admit a quantifier/loop convergence by itself; it only rules out different receivers, iterators, or traversal sources.
implementation_guidance: Require same-source provenance for the quantifier and loop traversal.
Reject different iterable bindings, mutated receivers, and derived iterables whose order/cardinality relation is not proven.
Let each frontend emit receiver/place evidence for its language surface.
rejected_evidence: different iterable bindings or receiver places
receiver or iterator mutation during traversal
derived iterables whose cardinality/order relationship is not proven
facts.summary: The quantifier and explicit loop must traverse the same source in the same order before their predicates can be compared.
facts.title: Iteration same-source identity

accepted_evidence: local comparisons over the loop or quantifier element and literals
no calls, assignments, yields, awaits, mutations, or logging inside the predicate or loop body
no observed state before the early return or inside the quantifier predicate
facts.detector_admission_implication: Does not admit a quantifier/loop convergence by itself; it only permits comparing short-circuit boundaries after predicate effects are closed.
implementation_guidance: Treat helper calls, mutation, logging, yield, await, and assignment as closed unless separate purity/effect evidence exists.
Keep short-circuit timing as behavior-defining when side effects can be observed.
Attach language surfaces through effect evidence producers or admitted purity resolvers.
rejected_evidence: predicate helper calls unless callee purity is proven
observed counters or logging before return
iterator, receiver, or captured-state mutation during traversal
facts.summary: The predicate must be pure enough that quantifier and loop short-circuiting observe the same effects and stop at the same first counterexample.
facts.title: Pure predicate/effect safety

accepted_evidence: comparison predicates whose results are booleans
the same element variable and the same literal/value coordinates on both sides
a boolean context where operand values are not observed
facts.detector_admission_implication: Retired compatibility alias; new packets must cite boolean.demorgan.proven-bool-operands.
implementation_guidance: Normalize De Morgan only for proven boolean operands.
Reject Python value-returning and/or contexts and effectful predicate calls.
rejected_evidence: Python value-returning and/or operands whose value, not only truthiness, is observed
overloaded comparison or predicate calls with effects
changed predicates such as x != 0 or x != 1
facts.summary: The counterexample guard not P may normalize through De Morgan only for proven boolean operands, for example not (x == 0 or x == 1) == (x != 0 and x != 1).
facts.title: Boolean-only De Morgan

accepted_evidence: local comparisons over the loop variable and literals
no calls, assignments, yields, awaits, or mutations inside the predicate or loop body
no observed state before the early return or inside the all(...) predicate
facts.detector_admission_implication: Retired compatibility alias; new packets must cite effect.pure-predicate.
implementation_guidance: Treat helper calls, mutation, logging, yield, await, and assignment as closed unless separate purity/effect evidence exists.
Keep short-circuit timing as behavior-defining when side effects can be observed.
rejected_evidence: predicate helper calls such as is_bad(x) unless callee purity is proven
observed counters or logging before return
iterator or receiver mutation during traversal
facts.summary: The predicate must be pure and exact-safe so all(...) short-circuit and the early-return loop observe the same effects and stop at the same first counterexample.
facts.title: Loop/all effect safety

accepted_evidence: all(...) and the explicit loop consume the same local iterable binding
no reassignment or mutation changes the iterable between the two forms
the generator and loop use the same element variable coordinate
facts.detector_admission_implication: Retired compatibility alias; new packets must cite iteration.same-source-identity.
implementation_guidance: Require same local iterable provenance for all(...) and the loop.
Reject forms where all(...) ranges over xs but the loop ranges over ys or over a mutated receiver.
rejected_evidence: different iterable bindings
receiver or iterator mutation during traversal
derived iterables whose cardinality/order relationship is not proven
facts.summary: The generator consumed by all(...) and the explicit loop must traverse the same iterable in the same order.
facts.title: Loop/all iterator identity

accepted_evidence: a single for-loop over the same local iterable
only the counterexample branch returns False
fallthrough return is literal True
empty iterables return True in both forms
facts.detector_admission_implication: Retired compatibility alias; new packets must cite quantifier.universal.counterexample-loop and quantifier.vacuous-truth.
implementation_guidance: Model the explicit loop as universal quantification only when the counterexample branch is the sole early False return and fallthrough returns literal True.
Keep wrong empty-input truth and extra loop control/effects closed.
rejected_evidence: fallthrough returns False or a non-boolean payload
loop body has break, continue, else effects, or extra observed state
the loop consumes a different iterable or mutates the iterable
facts.summary: A Python early-return loop that returns False on the first counterexample and True after exhaustion is equivalent to all(P(x) for x in xs) only with vacuous truth and matching short-circuit behavior.
facts.title: Universal loop short-circuit and vacuous truth

status_vocabulary.admitted-real-pair: The fact is reusable and has current real-pair evidence, but detector admission still depends on every fact required by the packet.
status_vocabulary.modeled-controlled: The fact is implemented or machine-checked for controlled evidence; individual real-corpus members still need source evidence.
status_vocabulary.retired: The fact id is retained only for historical artifacts and should not be cited by new packets.
status_vocabulary.specified-not-modeled: The fact is specified as a reusable prerequisite, but no detector/proof implementation can consume it yet.
